songs.title: Rebuilt
songs.seasonMoment: a late-October morning, first cold air of the season on a rebuilt station square
songs.listenerSituation: walking out of the hometown station the first morning back after nine years, finally answering a message left unanswered that whole time

VOCAL FIRST: mature warm female alto, centered low-mid chest support, forward mask resonance, 89% tone / 11% air, clean consonants, intimate conversational onset, restrained melisma only at phrase ends, chorus stays chest-led and wider through resonance rather than pitch. No semitone lift. Keep the rebuilt-station story close and human. Complete verse, pre, chorus, verse, 12-bar wordless break and final chorus; 3:10-3:25, no early cut.
songs.excludePrompt: bright soprano lead, airy head-voice glide, falsetto climax, semitone lift, octave jump, belted chorus, giant vocal stack, generic pop ballad, trap hi-hat rolls, EDM drop, heavy sidechain pumping, harsh top end, muddy sub bass, excessive reverb, hard autotune, karaoke backing, generic AI demo-band sound, early ending before final chorus
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Nine years and the rotary's a different shape,
Bus bays where the taxi stand used to be.
You asked me something once, I never wrote back,
Not because I didn't have the words,
I had them, I just kept them in a drawer.
Now I'm here with a bag and a cold coffee.

[Pre-Chorus]
The bakery's a bank, the bank's a phone shop,
Somebody repainted the whole street,
Ten seconds, that's all it ever needed,
And I still owe you one small honest answer,

[Chorus]
Sorry It Took So Long,
I carried it around from town to town,
Nine years of almost, and here it is,
No excuse that holds up in the daylight,
Plain as the sun coming up on this square.

[Verse 2]
Your name is still saved the way I saved it,
Under a nickname nobody else would get.
The station coffee tastes the same at least,
I could walk to your door in seven minutes,
Or I could type it out and press the thing.
I do both, in the end, in that order.

[Instrumental Break - 12 bars]

[Final Chorus]
Sorry It Took So Long,
I carried it around from town to town,
No excuse that holds up in the daylight,
The rotary is new, the answer isn't,
It waited in me all the way back home,
Sorry It Took So Long.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 8 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Two in the morning and the queue is empty,
The screen keeps offering songs to nobody.
Nobody's queued a song in half an hour,
Six of us, one couch, three of us asleep,
You're holding the mic like it's a cup of tea.
I ask you nothing. I've stopped asking, honestly.

[Pre-Chorus]
Then you turn the volume down a notch,
And the room gets small enough to hear you,

[Chorus]
You Said It Anyway,
Two hundred days after I gave up waiting,
Right there between the last two songs on the list,
No one looking, no one making a moment of it.

[Instrumental Break - 8 bars]

[Verse 2]
Somebody's jacket is over the coin box,
The last order came and went an hour back,
The clock above the door says we've got twenty.
You use my name the way you would use it sober,
Then the rest of it, quick, like you'd practiced.

[Pre-Chorus]
Then you turn the volume down a notch,
And the room gets small enough to hear you,

[Chorus]
Two hundred days after I gave up waiting,
Right there between the last two songs on the list,
No one looking, no one making a moment of it,
You Said It Anyway,

[Final Chorus]
You Said It Anyway,
Two hundred days after I gave up waiting,
The screen still glowing on an empty queue,
No one looking, no one making a moment of it,
You Said It Anyway.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Grey box, blue cursor, two years of dust on it,
Your thumb finds the folder without being told.
Takeaway container cold beside the laptop,
One lamp doing the work of a whole room.
Five paragraphs you wrote at twenty-four,
The subject line still says the same three words,
Every sentence true and none of them sent.

[Pre-Chorus]
You read it once, you don't read it twice,
Nothing in here is going to age better,
The person it was for has moved twice since,

[Chorus]
Rain going sideways past the window frame,
Still in the Box,
Blue light on a face that's older now,
Two winters folded into forty lines,
Your finger hovering, then not hovering.

[Verse 2]
The screen dims once and you wake it with a knuckle,
Outside a scooter drags its noise down the street.
The building hums the way it always hums,
You could send it now and make it somebody's problem,
Or you could close the tab and let it be yours.
Steam off a cup you forgot you poured out,

[Instrumental Break - 12 bars]

[Final Chorus]
Still in the Box,
Rain going sideways past the window frame,
Blue light on a face that's older now,
Two winters folded into forty lines,
Your finger hovering, then gone,
Let it go, let it go now,
Still in the Box.

[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1]
Low ceiling, one bulb over the pool table,
Your laugh comes across before your face does.
Same coat, different haircut, same way of standing,
Glass in your left hand like you always did.
Somebody's coat is on the chair beside me,
I count to five behind my own drink,
Crowd moves and there you are again.

[Pre-Chorus]
Two exits, one of them is easy,
The distance is eleven steps of carpet,
The other one costs about ten seconds,
I've spent three years not spending them,

[Chorus]
Three Years Too Late,
Halfway across a room that isn't ours,
I cross the floor and say your name out loud,
No speech, no reason, nothing to defend,
Just the word I should have said in a doorway once.

[Verse 2]
You blink and then you smile like it's normal,
You wondered, you tell me, but not how often.
We stand there where the music's slightly quieter,
Two strangers with the same old inside joke.
Nothing lands the way I rehearsed it,
Which is fine, which is better, honestly.

[Instrumental Break - 12 bars]

[Final Chorus]
Three Years Too Late,
Halfway across a room that isn't ours,
I cross the floor and say your name out loud,
No speech, no reason, nothing to defend,
The bar goes on and neither of us leaves,
Three Years Too Late.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
One More Coin,

[Verse 1]
Fluorescent white and a wall of plastic prizes,
The prize tags curl where the tape lets go,
The carpet is sticky and none of us minds,
Three of us leaning on the glass at two,
Coins in a paper cup between us,
The claw comes down polite and lets it go,
Somebody groans, somebody buys another go.
You're not even trying to win the thing.

[Chorus]
One More Coin,
Nobody here is going home a winner.

[Verse 2]
You say it while the arm is swinging back,
The thing I asked you at the end of winter,
Half a year of you not knowing how,
And now it's out between a bear and a duck.
The music in here has been the same all night,
You keep your eyes right on the glass, and I let you.

[Instrumental Break - 12 bars]

[Bridge]
Nobody in this arcade heard a thing,
The change machine takes a note and thinks about it,
Outside it is cold and in here it is not,
Somebody's sleeve is stuck against the button,
And I'm holding a coin I'm not going to spend,
Because you already gave me the answer,
Because you finally said it out loud.

[Final Chorus]
One More Coin,
Nobody here is going home a winner,
And I've never lost so happily in my life,
One More Coin.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four Small Frames,

[Verse 1]
You clear out the old wallet for the bin,
And a strip falls out folded twice at the crease.
First frame, you're mid-sentence, eyes half shut.
Second frame, somebody's hand on your shoulder.
Third frame, all four of you are laughing wrong.
Fourth frame, nobody's looking at the camera.
On the back in blue pen, seven digits and a name.

[Chorus]
Ink gone soft, paper gone thin,
Four Small Frames,
Somebody's thumb across the top left corner,
A number you never once dialled,
Ten years asleep in a leather fold.

[Verse 2]
You sit down on the floor beside the bin bag,
The bag stays open, the floor stays cold,
You do the maths and the maths is not kind.
The strip is warm from being in your hand,
Ten years and the digits are still legible,
You read the name out loud to nobody,
It sounds exactly like it used to sound,
You could say it's too long now to matter,
Or you could put the strip up on the shelf,
And type the seven digits in tonight.

[Breakdown - 8 bars instrumental]

[Final Chorus]
Four Small Frames,
Ink gone soft, paper gone thin,
Somebody's thumb across the top left corner,
A number you never once dialled,
Ringing out in a room that's warm again,
Four Small Frames.

[Intro]
I'll Send It Today,

[Verse 1]
Five-fifty, and the street is only pigeons,
Six-forty, and the first shutter goes up,
Six-fifty, crates of greens on the wet stone,
Seven, a hose runs a line down the middle,
Eight, and the first customer wants change,
Ten past, the fish man argues with a van,
Quarter past, the bakery lets out its smell,
Seven-thirty, and my hands stop being cold.

[Chorus]
Delivery bikes leaning on the railing,
Awnings coming down along the row,
Steam off the stone where the water ran,
I'll Send It Today,
Four months in a coat pocket, that's enough.

[Verse 2]
Ask me why it took a season, honestly,
I'll tell you I was busy, which is a lie.
The truth is smaller and it doesn't sound good:
I was scared of what a stamp makes permanent.
Somebody sweeps a doorway, says good morning,
I say it back and mean it, for once,
Nine minutes of walking left in me,
Half past, and the postbox is red ahead.

[Instrumental Break - 10 bars]

[Final Chorus]
I'll Send It Today,
Delivery bikes leaning on the railing,
Awnings coming down along the row,
Steam off the stone where the water ran,
Four months in a coat pocket, that's enough,
(Go on now, let it go)

[Verse 1]
Empty four lanes and the whole width is mine,
Chain ticking, jacket open, hands loose,

Third draft by the bridge, fourth by the park,

Send It at the Light,

[Intro - 4 bars instrumental]

[Verse 1]
He watches the last set of tail-lights leave the platform,
Then the board goes blank and stays blank.
The platform empties by ones, then by nobody,
A cleaner works the far end with a wide broom,
The gates roll down in three slow sections.
He sits because there's nothing else to do,
And takes the phone out for the first time in an hour.

[Pre-Chorus]
There's a message from last February in there,
He's read it more times than he's admitted,

[Chorus]
A Year Late,

He types a line and deletes it and types it again,
Thumbs slower than his thinking, which is new.

The station lets him have the whole hour,
Nothing is going to arrive until five,
Nobody hurrying him toward a decision,
He presses send and puts the phone face down,

A Year Late,
Steel shutters down over an empty gate,
Chewing gum ghosts on a cold tiled floor,
One man breathing out, one small screen dark,

[Verse 1]
One lamp, one desk, the flat gone dark behind me,
Headphones off one ear so the room stays real.
I've typed you four answers and killed each one,
Words go stiff on me the second they're written,
So I move the laptop, and I move the cup,
And I do the only thing that ever works.

[Chorus]
Say It Out Loud,
No draft, no edit, no clever second pass,
One take, and I'm sending the one take,
Just my voice at one in the morning going,
Here's what I meant, eight months ago, plainly.

[Verse 2]
You'll hear the radiator in the background,
You'll hear me stop and start and lose the thread,
It's not tidy, it's not the version I planned,
But you'll hear the truth in the way it wobbles,
I'd rather be heard than sound like I'm fine,
And I do the only thing that ever works.

[Bridge]
Twelve seconds. Then thirty. Then a minute ten.
Nobody's grading this, nobody's listening yet,
The little red circle doesn't care how I sound,
And I keep going until it's actually finished.

[Instrumental Break - 10 bars]

[Final Chorus]
Say It Out Loud,
No draft, no edit, no clever second pass,
One take, and I'm sending the one take,
Take it however it lands, it's honest,
Say It Out Loud.

I Should Have Said It,

[Verse 1]
Two stools, a counter built for elbows only,
Steam climbing where the pots come off the ring,
Half eleven, and the shutter's already half down,
You order first because you always order first.
Two orders in and the shop is only us,
The window over the counter is fogged solid,
I talk to the wood in front of me, not you:
About the weather, then the trains, then March.
Somewhere in there the difficult part gets out.

[Chorus]
Chopsticks flat across a chipped white rim,
I Should Have Said It.

[Verse 2]
You don't turn your head, which I'm grateful for,
You say one word and it's the right one.
The cook drops a basket and nobody jumps.
A delivery bike goes past and neither of us looks,
Your sleeve is wet where you leaned in the sink,
Six months of me carrying a sentence around,
The counter takes it the way wood takes rain,
Nothing in this shop cares what we decide,
We can talk about it properly later, you tell me.

[Breakdown - 8 bars instrumental]

[Final Chorus]
I Should Have Said It,
Chopsticks flat across a chipped white rim,
Two coats on one hook, steam on the glass,
Six months, and the counter took it fine,
I Should Have Said It.

[Verse 1]
Tomorrow, I keep telling myself, tomorrow.
Concourse noise coming up off the tiles,
Locker two-fourteen, second row, near the stairs,
The key's been warm in this pocket for a month.
Announcements land and slide off me again,
There's a letter in that bag with my name wrong,
And an answer in me that I haven't written.

[Pre-Chorus]
Tomorrow sounds like a place I could live in,
Six months of tomorrow adds up to zero,
It has a door and I keep walking past it,

[Chorus]
Answer It Tomorrow,
That's what I said in April, and in May,
The board flips over, changes nothing for me,
A key is a small thing to be afraid of.

[Verse 2]
Tomorrow, I try it once more and hear it,
It sounds thinner out loud than in my head.
Ask me what I'm scared of, go on, ask me,
I'll get it wrong first, and then I'll get it right:
I'm not scared of the letter, I'm scared it's fair.
So I turn around, and I go get the bag.

[Instrumental Break - 12 bars]

[Final Chorus]
Answer It Tomorrow,
That's what I said in April, and in May,
Not this time, not one more month of it,
The locker opens easier than I thought,
Answer It Tomorrow.

You Wrote Back,

[Verse 1]
Eight-ten, and the platform is one animal,

You Wrote Back,

And the crowd goes soft around the edges.

Undone by nine words on a Tuesday,
I'm laughing at a departure board like a fool,

Right here, in the middle of two thousand people,
Sorry it took so long, you wrote, and then the rest,

You Wrote Back,

You Wrote Back,
Right here, in the middle of two thousand people,
I've got nine years of things to tell you,
